articleTitle: Computer Vision-Based Home Accident Detection and Response System for Elderly Care
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper proposes a computer vision-based system to address the pressing need for comprehensive home accident detection and response for the elderly. The system aims to fill the existing research gaps by expanding accident detection coverage and improving accident response procedures. The system receives the input real-time videos from a 2D RGB camera captured in indoor scenes, detects single-person accidents, stores the accident recordings, and sends alert messages. In the proposed framework, pose estimation is applied to extract the appearance feature, namely the elderly's skeleton key points from the input videos using MediaPipe Holistic. This feature is then input to the long short-term memory (LSTM) deep learning model to categorize the elderly's activities into falls, choking, and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) which indicate the absence of accidents. The framework is evaluated on UR Fall Detection (URFD) dataset and a self-generated dataset. The result shows that the framework achieved an accuracy of 87% in fall detection, 77% in choking detection, and 83% in ADL detection.

articleTitle: The Science of Video: A Review of Human Activity Recognition Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) from video data has gained significant attention due to its wide-ranging applications in fields like security surveillance, healthcare, and human-computer interaction. Recognizing and categorizing human behaviours and movements from video footage is a challenging task due to the complexity and diversity of human actions. Real-time processing is essential for HAR systems to effectively monitor and analyse human behaviours in real-world contexts. This study aims to analyse different HAR method and enumerate and talk about the difficulties and restrictions of the methods used for HAR nowadays. The significance of this study lies in its potential to enhance safety, security, healthcare monitoring, and human-computer interaction by addressing key challenges in HAR and paving the way for future advancements and applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Phishing Website Detection: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: In the 21st century, majority of the population in the world are connected to the Internet as the Internet allows them to do various of activities with just one click. However, with the growing prevalence of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and increased internet usage, cyberattacks are increasing in an alarming state especially phishing attacks. Hence, in this research, a hybrid approach, which combines URL-based model and content-based model, was conducted. A total of four models, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Naïve Bayes (NB) and ensemble models were implemented in this research. Three datasets were applied, and it turned out that the proposed hybrid approach performed better than the non-hybrid approaches. The best performing model for the hybrid approach was the RF model which achieved the accuracy of 95.3% and the False Positive Rate (FPR) and False Negative Rate (FNR) of 5.4% and 3.9% respectively. Besides that, it was concluded that the ensemble model was able to detect phishing websites accurately by achieving an accuracy score of 94.7%, a FPR of 5.9% and a FNR of 4.7%.

articleTitle: Data Driven Analysis of Fraudulent Transaction Characteristics in Branchless Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: In branchless banking, fraudulent transactions can be defined as an act of an agent to conduct some non-essential transactions to receive transaction's fee. This transaction is a legitimate transaction, in terms of money movement. It is hard to detect the fraudulent transaction in this manner. This study aims to learn about the characteristics of a fraudulent transaction and provide a rule for determining suspected fraudulent transaction. To reduce the size of transactions data, Leiden community detection algorithms is used. The user is clustered in a transactional graph data. Each community is then statistically processed to acquire the outlier. From the analysis it is estimated that 25% of agent has done fraudulent transactions. The fraudulent transaction characteristic was expressed in term of the average of the community. The fraudulent transactions are 185% above the average in terms of transactions value. While for the transaction frequency, the fraudulent transactions are 90% above the average frequency. The fraudulent transactions data always act as an outlier in their respective community.

articleTitle: Restaurant Recommendations with Implicit User Behavior via Image Classification and Sentiment Analysis from Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Traditional recommendation systems often fall short in understanding users' true food preferences on social media platforms. This paper introduces an innovative approach to enhance the dining experience by leveraging implicit user behavior via image classification and sentiment analysis. The proposed system combines food image classification (MobileNetV2) and sentiment analysis (Transformer Flair) on social media comments, creating a robust framework for implicit recommendation. The results demonstrate the system's efficacy in accurately predicting food categories and extracting positive sentiments from user comments. By systematically linking these insights to user profiles, the paper establishes a recommendation system that considers both culinary preferences and geographical location. The seamless integration of computer vision and natural language processing allows for a more tailored and personalized restaurant suggestion, addressing the limitations of existing recommendation systems. The research highlights the potential of harnessing implicit user data from social media to revolutionize the landscape of personalized dining recommendations, setting the stage for future advancements in understanding and adapting to users' evolving preferences.

articleTitle: Exploring Part-of-Speech Tagging Models in Malaysia's Multilingual
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This study delves into the realm of part-of-speech (POS) tagging within Malaysia's multilingual context. We investigate the efficacy of CRF-QTAG, semi-supervised CRF models and rule-based systems within Bahasa Rojak Analytics—a Malay-based language processing system. By analyzing these models' performances, we observed the profound impact of retraining on their accuracy. While CRF-QTAG and semi-supervised CRF models showcased substantial improvements post-retraining, the rigidity of the rule-based system led to underperformance. The study sheds light on challenges posed by linguistic nuances in code-mixed languages and the dependence on labeled data. Our findings highlight the potential of semi-supervised models in addressing data scarcity issues and adapting to linguistic evolution. Additionally, we advocate for further research aimed at refining rule-based approaches by emphasizing linguistic comprehension and rule definition for enhanced adaptability and accuracy. Addressing these challenges can potentially pave the way for more inclusive and precise language technologies tailored to Malaysia's diverse linguistic fabric.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning in Medical Diagnostics: An Examination of SimCLR and BYOL in Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Supervised learning algorithms have accomplished significant advancements in the field of medical image classification. However, these methods highly rely on large labelled datasets and it is costly to obtain image datasets with proper labels. To solve this issue, contrastive learning aims to learn representations by contrasting positive and negative examples by maximising the similarity between positive pairs and minimising the similarity between negative pairs. In this paper, the performance of two prominent contrastive self-supervised learning (SSL) frameworks, SimCLR and BYOL, will be compared in the specific context of medical image classification using the CheXpert dataset. ResNet-18, is used as the model backbone for comparison purposes for its low compute requirements and common usage for image classification. The result shows that SimCLR provides the best performance compared to BYOL with hardware constraints. However, neither of which outperform current supervised models due to limited hyperparameter configurations. The objectives of this paper is to overcome the challenges of limited availability and high costs of annotated data in medical image classification by using self-supervised learning techniques, to enhance the performance of image classification models by effectively utilising unlabelled medical images, and to assess the performance and drawbacks associated with different self-supervised learning frameworks.

articleTitle: Evaluating Translation Quality and Usability of Maana: A Meranaw-English Bidirectional Speech Translation App
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of Maana, a novel Meranaw-English bidirectional speech translation application designed to bridge linguistic gaps and preserve the Meranaw language in the Philippines. Given that Meranaw is a low-resource language, we utilize a modest training dataset to fine-tune a pretrained transformer model. Maana demonstrates commendable translation accuracy, validated through both automated metrics like BLEU and METEOR and comprehensive human evaluations. Maana integrates Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Machine Translation (MT), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) functionalities within a user-friendly web interface. The app's usability evaluated through System Usability Scale (SUS) indicates high user satisfaction, reflecting the app's effectiveness and ease of use in facilitating cross-cultural communication. This research not only emphasizes Maana's role in language preservation but also showcases its innovative approach in the field of language translation technology.

articleTitle: Building Trust in E-Commerce by Examining the Relationships Between User Experience and Delivery Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This study analyzes the relationship across user experience, delivery satisfaction, and trust within the domain of e-commerce. The variables are assessed using Partial Least Squares (PLS) to identify their interaction. This research utilised a survey approach for collecting data from a sample of 151 participants, with the intent of interpreting their points of view. The findings suggest a significant correlation across user experience and trust in the framework of online purchase. Moreover, this study demonstrates that the satisfaction of customers with the delivery process plays a role in the creation of trust, but to a lesser extent compared to the user experience. These findings provide useful insights into the approaches that online platforms could utilize to establish and maintain the trust of their users.

articleTitle: Unveiling Bahasa Rojak's Linguistic Complexity: Out-of-Vocabulary Detection and Tokenization Strategies for Language
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This study dives into the subtle realm of Bahasa Rojak focusing on the critical function of Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) detection tasks in unraveling its dense linguistic tapestry. The study uses painstaking preprocessing methods to improve the textual data after gathering data from various sources. The study uses Brown Clustering to find linguistic trends and groupings within the Bahasa Rojak language. Furthermore, this work dissects and encodes complicated lexical elements using several tokenization methods—Byte Pair Encoding (BPE), Unigram, Word Piece, and Sentence Piece—revealing numerous segmentation views. The goal is to create a Union Vocabulary that combines different segments while minimizing duplication, hence lowering OOV occurrences. The combination of these strategies not only improves language representation but also demonstrates the adaptability and usefulness of various tokenization techniques in dealing with OOV terms. This investigation provides insights into effective ways for dealing with OOV terms in linguistic datasets.

articleTitle: The Mediating Role of Cobit 2019 in Managing the Relationship Between Qualitative Characteristics of Accounting Information and Information Asymmetry
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper aims to determine how COBIT 2019 Framework (COB) and Quality Characteristics of Accounting Information (QC) affect Information Asymmetry (IA). The sample of this paper was the employees of the Commercial Bank of Iraq (CBIQ). These employees were surveyed and 99 valid e-questionnaires were used to gather data. Smart-PLS analysis was employed to establish reliability and validity and to evaluate the put out hypotheses. The findings showed that COB can play an influential role to reduce IA, and Organizations should prioritize improving the qualitative qualities of information because doing so can benefit both COB implementation and the decrease of IA. In addition, COB implementation can serve as a strategic strategy to harmonizing qualitative information features with the purpose of eliminating IA. However, this paper can help the employees to reduce the IA by producing good quality accounting information via COB.

articleTitle: Enhancing Child Safety: Computer Vision-Based Accident Detection for Infants and Toddlers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Children, who are infants and toddlers are prone to accidents when not supervised. Children may wander off and get hurt, such as falling from high places, getting burns, and more. Falls and drops are a major cause of injuries among children in the United States (US), with over 2.8 million children treated in emergency rooms each year. Parents need to always supervise the children but finding a balance with work can be challenging. The proposed system uses closed-circuit television (CCTV) and machine learning to detect two common types of accidents: cuts, and burns. The proposed system identifies children and dangerous objects, tracks movements, captures frames, and estimate the risk. The system offers a comprehensive solution to children monitoring, reducing accidents, and providing parents with peace of mind. The results show that detection accuracies are 87%, 84% and 75% for scissors, knife and both items respectively. The project findings indicate that the detection of accident risks achieves a satisfactory level of accuracy. However, when multiple dangerous objects are present in the field of view, the accuracy experiences a slight decline.

articleTitle: Parallel Computing Using CUDA and MultiThreading in Background Removal Process
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Parallel processing involves challenges on data dependency. In this work, we presented an investigation of performance into image background removal using the Rembg algorithms incorporating parallel computing techniques including Multithreading and Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA). In the background subtraction algorithm, each pixel of the image is compared with the pixels around it. Thus, it will be difficult to parallelise the system if the pixel is being accessed at the same time; otherwise, it will lead to data corruption or inconsistent results. CUDA and Multithreading are utilised in 2, 4 and 8 threads on two different hardware specification machines. Results show the proposed work achieves a maximum of 5.3092 and 5.7913 speed up value in CUDA and Multithreading respectively. In a nutshell, dynamic thread allocation and advanced load balancing algorithms that adapt to changing workloads in real-time can ensure that the computational workload is distributed evenly among threads and GPU cores.

articleTitle: Enhancing Music Emotion Classification with Lyrics and Audio Features
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: The role of automatic generated playlists and recommendations in music streaming services has played a significant role in driving the steady growth of the music industry since 2015. With the evolving landscape of music, Music Emotion Recognition (MER) has gained importance in this era. Contemporary solutions today focus solely on four emotions and popular music genres, neglecting emerging styles and artistes where their music evokes a danceable rhythm, but lyrics convey negativity. This study considers both lyrics and audio features for the classification of eight emotions with the aim to identify key features influencing music emotion, develop a classification model and evaluate its performance. A dataset was created by expanding a base dataset with additional lyrics and audio features from Genius and Spotify API respectively. This study employs established algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Decision Trees (DT), and Random Forests (RF), with Random Forests emerging with a notable 73% accuracy. A web application named Emotion was developed, allowing data scientists and music researchers to explore the dataset and access details of this study. This study's impact extends to various applications, including mental health and media, enabling tailored music-based interventions for emotional well-being, and improving music selection in media and entertainment.

articleTitle: Identification of Skin Conditions with Convolutional Neural Networks: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper presents a robust approach for detecting skin diseases using advanced image detection methods supported by Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. Traditionally, skin diseases are diagnosed by experienced dermatologists. However, due to a scarcity of these specialists, there is a pressing need for alternative, reliable solutions. Our methodology capitalizes on image detection techniques to accurately and efficiently identify potential skin diseases from photographs. The cornerstone of our approach is the CNN model, which is renowned for its efficacy in processing visual data. The system we developed demonstrates a high level of accuracy, achieving a validation accuracy of at least 80 % in the identification of specific skin diseases. This level of precision is particularly noteworthy, considering the inherent challenges in diagnosing skin conditions through images. Despite this success, our research also acknowledges the difficulties in gathering a vast, diverse dataset of skin disease images from the internet. Such datasets are crucial for training and refining our model to ensure its effectiveness across various skin types and conditions. Furthermore, this paper investigates the factors that might lead to inaccuracies in predictions. It addresses common issues such as variations in image quality, lighting conditions, and the presence of similar-looking skin conditions, which can all potentially confound the model's decision-making process. By understanding and mitigating these factors, we aim to enhance the model's reliability and accuracy, moving closer to bridging the gap between automated detection and expert human diagnosis. This research not only contributes to the field of medical image analysis but also offers a promising tool for assisting dermatologists and improving patient outcomes in skin disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Multiword Expression Extraction on Chinese-English Code-Mixed Malaysian Expressions on E-commerce Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Multiword Expression (MWE) extraction has been popular research in Natural Language Processing (NLP) area. This research aims to extract different MWE types, including Chinese (ZH), English (EN), Chinese-English (ZH-EN) code-mixed, and new word MWEs, from Malaysian Expressions (MSEs) in the e-commerce platform. MSEs are multilingual and contain code-mixed text as well as Out-Of-Vocabulary (OOV). Thus, they are highly unstructured. A comparative study is conducted using various statistical models such as Branch Entropy (BE), Normalized Branch Entropy (NBE) and Accessor Variety (AV). Each statistical model's performance is assessed using Top N precision. The study reveals the characteristics of ZH-EN code-mixed MSEs in e-commerce platforms and the contribution of punctuation towards the Top N precision of statistical models. The experiment results show that AV outperforms BE variations, whereas NBE outperforms conventional BE.

articleTitle: Designing an Adaptive Learning Management System at AMA Computer Learning College–ORMOC (ACLC): Development and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: An Adaptive Learning Management System (LMS) is a transformative platform that integrates adaptive learning principles and technologies, revolutionizing the educational experience. This study focuses on designing an adaptive LMS tailored to Java programming, evaluating student engagement, and gauging perceptions of system features. With 51 respondents (26 males, 25 females), the study showcases the platform's capacity to actively involve students, capturing sustained attention through tools like CodeRunner, adaptive quizzes, and H5P interactive features. This heightened engagement significantly contributes to positive learning outcomes and overall student success. The adaptive LMS not only exceeds student expectations but also provides a personalized, flexible learning experience, addressing diverse learning styles and preferences. The system's effectiveness promotes inclusivity, thereby reducing educational disparities. These findings underscore the pivotal role of technology in modern education and advocate for a transformative approach to programming education.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing the Adoption and Usage of E-Wallets
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: In today's digital era, financial transactions have witnessed a significant shift with the advent of digital payment methods. Among these, E-wallets have emerged as a popular choice, offering users a convenient and secure means of managing their finances. As E-wallet adoption continues to rise, it is crucial to explore the factors that drive users to incorporate E-wallets into their daily routines. The key factors identified in this paper can serve as an opportunity for financial service providers to enhance their services, thereby persuading individuals to adopt digital payments in the future. This research uses a qualitative method with a systematic literature review approach, we identified 30 factors from a pool of 52 selected papers. Among these factors, 13 fall under the personal category, while 6 are categorized as technological. Additionally, it's noteworthy that the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) emerged as the most frequently utilized research model in these 52 papers, featuring in 18 of them. In conclusion, perceived security, take the most influential factor in adopting E-Wallet.

articleTitle: A Knowledge-Based System of Ethno-Medicinal Plants in Lanao Del Sur for Treating Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of the ethno-medicinal knowledge in Lanao del Sur, a region rich in biodiversity and culture. Focusing on the traditional uses of plants for therapeutic purposes, the study integrates indigenous knowledge with modern technology to develop a knowledge-based system for recommending ethno-medicinal plants to treat common diseases. Knowledge had been acquired from local people with expertise in ethnomedicinal practices; that acquired knowledge would be translated into rules that can be read by the rule engine; and after translating all the knowledge into rules, it would be tested for its correctness in recommendation. This interdisciplinary approach contributes to the preservation of traditional knowledge and opens avenues for sustainable healthcare practices that bridge the gap between traditional wisdom and contemporary science. The paper advocates for recognizing and integrating ethno-medicinal practices into mainstream healthcare systems, fostering a harmonious coexistence of cultural heritage and modern advancements in medical science within Lanao del Sur and beyond.

articleTitle: Oral Disease Image Detection System Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to detect oral disease using image detection method. Oral disease is usually checked with the presence of dentist, however, with the trend of dentist growing slower and slower, a solution is needed to overcome such problem. Our methodology uses the image recognition technique to visually detect any possible oral disease from the uploaded picture. There are total seven oral disease will be tested in this research which are calculus, data caries, gingivitis, hypodontia, mouth ulcer, oral cancer and discoloration. The system achieved a validation accuracy rate of at least 80% in detecting specified oral disease. However, certain limitations were identified, such as challenges to obtain sufficient datasets from the internet. This paper also discusses the implications and prospects of extending this approach to accommodate a wider range of oral disease that can be visually examined.

articleTitle: Utterance Intent Recognition for Online Retail
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: In Indonesian business environments, vital information required for operations is often available from centralized sources or through direct connection with relevant departments. Despite accessible information channels, stakeholders such as customers, business owners, and other parties frequently contact organizations directly to request confirmation or additional information. The volume of questions varies with the company's size, providing difficulty for larger enterprises. This buildup of questions frequently causes delays in responding to information demands. This research focuses on constructing chatbots developed with using chat feature conversation obtained from an e-commerce platform. As a result, the goal of this research is to build a task-oriented chatbot model tailored to enterprises, with the goal of efficiently addressing user queries within the chatbot's domain. The intent classification task is trained with a Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural network architecture utilizing the Adam optimizer. This study investigates models for categorizing agent and visitor intentions for chatbot interaction between customer and business owner, demonstrating a 65% accuracy in agent intent and a 74% accuracy in visitor intent. The study highlighted the overfitting challenge in intent classification, implying that improving minority intent categories should be prioritized to avoid such concerns and improve model quality.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Versus High-Intensity Exercise on Renal Biomarkers in Athletes: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Exercise offers significant health benefits, promoting normal body system functioning, healthy growth, development, and overall well-being. The objective of the present study was to determine the effect of high and low intensity exercise on renal biomarkers acute response in athletes. This cross sectional study was carried out in the department of physical education, Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi (UP). A total of 20 healthy male athletes with age range from 22 to 26 years were randomly selected. All subjects performed high and low intensity exercise for 5 minutes with a gap of 7 days. Blood samples for selected renal biomarkers were collected at pre-exercise, immediately after exercise, 10 and 20 minutes after the high and low intensity exercise. The serum urea and creatinine count decreased significantly after high-intensity exercise compared to low-intensity exercise (p<0.05). When compared to the baseline, this effect was still observable after ten and twenty minutes of passive recovery (p<0.05). There was a substantial increase in serum sodium and potassium from baseline immediately after exercise (p<0.05), after ten and twenty minutes of passive recovery without reaching to baseline. When the same subjects were exposed to different exercise intensities, the acute and short-term effects of exercise on renal biomarkers were intensity-dependent immediately after exercise, after ten and twenty minutes of passive recovery.

articleTitle: SentiWordNet and LDA Analysis of Foreign Tourist
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This research aims to explore and understand the sentiments and concerns of foreign tourists visiting Borobudur, Indonesia, through the application of sentiment analysis and LDA modeling on textual reviews. The sentiment analysis using SentiWordNet, and LDA topic modeling to identify key topics. Initial results highlight five prominent negative topics, including concerns about overcrowding, animal welfare, temple preservation, differentiated ticket prices, and interactions with sellers.

articleTitle: From Complexity to Clarity: Tatabahasa-Centric Lemmatization in Malay Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper explores the pivotal role of lemmatization tools in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and their significance in enhancing language understanding and text analysis. Through a comprehensive evaluation of various lemmatization techniques, both established and emerging, we aim to improve the precision of NLP applications. Our assessment encompasses diverse linguistic datasets, revealing insights into the strengths and limitations of each approach and guiding the selection of appropriate tools. What differentiates this study is its focus on the substantial advancement accomplished by the rule-based model, which exhibits an impressive 88% precision and outperforms the Sastrawi model by around 3%. Moreover, we introduce innovative strategies to enhance lemmatization outcomes, specifically addressing challenges in multilingual and low-resource language contexts.

articleTitle: Asset Modelling for Efficient Data Representation in Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Industry 4.0 presents considerable challenges in data unification. The Asset Administration Shell is a key concept introduced by Reference Architecture Model Industry 4.0 to enable the storage and communication of data between assets. The current conceptualization of the Asset Administration Shell exhibits limitations when it comes to representing digital data. It lacks an effective methodology for categorizing and defining existing data as an asset and this can potentially hinder the full utilization of digital data as an integral asset within the Industry 4.0 infrastructure. This research proposes an asset model inspired from Asset Administration Shell to better represent the ever-evolving digital data as a valuable asset within the Industry 4.0 framework.

articleTitle: Sign Language to Text Translation with Computer Vision: Bridging the Communication Gap
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This research paper addresses the communication barriers faced by individuals using sign language and those without hearing difficulties. With limited adoption of sign language and a scarcity of proficient human translators, there is a need for innovative solutions. This research presents a real-time sign language translation system using computer vision technology. The system utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for static and dynamic sign recognition, respectively. Word segmentation which utilized ‘word-ninja’ and a Large Language Model (LLM) contributed to accurate sentence generation. The proposed system integrates machine translation and text-to-speech functionalities to improve the system's accessibility. The methodology involves data collection, landmark recognition, and the implementation of recognition and translation models. The results show impressive accuracy which are 99.20% and 90.08% for static and dynamic sign recognition respectively. However, issues such as environmental conditions have affected the detection accuracy and made errors in recognising similar signs. Sentence generation also provided a pretty decent result which is 90% of the accuracy from the output provided by the LLM model. Despite these challenges, the system still contributes to reducing communication barriers and promoting inclusivity in society.

articleTitle: Adaptive IoT-Based Monitoring System in Edge Network for Aquaponics Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Aquaponics is a modern method of farming and cultivating fish. With the various advantages offered, this method has become popular with the public. Water quality is the key to success in using the aquaponics method. Farmers must monitor water quality regularly and continuously to ensure that water conditions still meet standards as a place for fish to live and contain sufficient nutrients for plant growth. To overcome this problem, an adaptive aquaponics system was created to retrieve and display the data automatically. This system will provide data every minute. The system will be IoT-based and adaptive. Adaptive here means the system can adapt to the state of the existing internet connection. So that the system can be more resilient in overcoming connection problems, and the collected data will not be lost when the system is disconnected from the internet.

articleTitle: Linguistic Harmony in Diversity: Lemmatizing Rojak Malay for Global Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to lemmatization and standardization of the Rojak Malay language. Rojak Malay, characterized by its amalgamation of Malay and English words, poses unique challenges for natural language processing (NLP). Our methodology leverages the combination of various techniques in a predefined order, including English lemmatization using WordNet, translation with GoogleTranslator, stemming using Sastrawi stemmer, normalization using BM_dict.csv dataset and Bahasa Malaysia lemmatization using Malaya to transform Rojak Malay into Standard Malay effectively. The system achieved an accuracy rate of 100% in lemmatizing a random sample of individual words. However, certain limitations were identified, such as challenges in handling code-mixed sentences and English out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words. This paper also discusses the implications and prospects of extending this approach to accommodate a wider range of languages found in the Rojak Malay context.

articleTitle: Exploring Varied Experiences of Foreign and Domestic Tourists at Borobudur through LDA Topic AnalysisIvan
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: The primary intention of this study is to explain and contrasting identifiable patterns related to the preferences and concerns expressed by foreign and domestic tourists during their visits to Borobudur, a well-known cultural monument located in Indonesia. Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) as the main methodology, a systematic assessment was conducted on scraped reviews obtained from from TripAdvisor, a popular travel review website in both English and Indonesian languages. The dataset, which contains a span of multiple years, went through preprocessing processes in order to ensure the cleanliness and validity of the data. The LDA topic modeling technique was then used to identify latent topics inherent in the reviews. The findings indicate substantial variations in the priorities and desires of foreign tourists compared to domestic tourists.

articleTitle: Investigation on Correlation of Water Quality Data with Aerial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Maintaining good water quality is fundamental for successful and sustainable pond fish farming. It directly affects the health, growth, and overall well-being of the fish population and contributes to the overall success of the aquaculture operation. Therefore, periodic control of water quality is highly recommended. The forthcoming methodology aims to assess water quality using aerial imagery. Nevertheless, to implement this approach, an initial inquiry is required to examine the correlation between aerial imagery and sensor data. In this scenario, data comprising TDS, pH, and temperature is acquired using manual sensors. Simultaneously, aerial images are captured using drones at different altitudes. Two approaches are employed to extract features from these aerial images: one involves determining the dominant eigenvalues of the image pixel matrix, and the other employs matrix convolution techniques, incorporating kernel matrices and max pooling matrix techniques. Subsequent to extracting the image feature data, correlation analysis is performed using the Spearman method. The result shows that there is a weak correlation between grayscale image and TDS level at 0.1 from eigenvalues method, and −0.30 from convolution method.

articleTitle: Laser Pointer-Ray Projection and Collision Detection for 3-Dimensional Shooting Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Nowadays, in police agencies and the military, shooting simulators are widely used to reduce the risk of danger due to operational errors and limited situational simulation. Several studies have proposed shooting simulators for shooting accuracy on paper targets or 2-dimensional (2D) while 3-dimensional (3D) shooting simulators can support specific situation-based training such as ambush and rescue scenarios with dynamic target movements. The previous research only discussed 3D shooting simulators by the general of the architecture and a glimpse of bullet trajectory but does not involve azimuth angle so shooting simulations cannot be carried out at several different horizontal angles. This research proposed in more detail the formula for calculating laser pointer-ray projection based on elevation and azimuth angles as well as collision detection. The results of the experiment showed that 47% of the shooting hit the small target from different horizontal angles whereas in the previous method, only 8% hit the target due to not involving azimuth angles. The shooting of the proposed method did not hit the target is caused by the small dimensions of the target made it difficult to aim for long distances. As such, the proposed method can enhance the variety of shooting training.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Evaluation of Online Appointment System at Mindanao State University–Main Campus: Employing the System Usability Scale (SUS) and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: During the epidemic, the Mindanao State University's Office of the President had numerous problems, including distant work and increased expectations. To address the long-standing inefficiencies in appointment handling, this study developed a web-based system. The study attempted to examine the effectiveness of the deployed system employing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and System Usability Scale (SUS). With an overall percentage of 90.2, the results show a noteworthy degree of customer satisfaction, confirming the effectiveness of the web-based appointment system. As a result, this creative approach has the potential to greatly reduce customer wait times at the Office of the President and enable more convenient employee appointment scheduling, which would be a major step toward more efficient administrative procedures.

Author Keywords: System Usability Scales and Technology Acceptance Model

articleTitle: Customer Propensity Model: Marketing Campaign
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: A marketing campaign being conducted undeniably consumes lots of resources and funds to be carried on. It is vital to ensure that such campaigns being conducted are effective and the resources used are not going in vain. Thus, it is important to recognise potential customers who might respond to the campaign and shrink the range of the target market. This research considers four different models, Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boost (XGBoost) and Extreme Gradient Boost Random Forest (XGBRF) to determine the best model for a propensity model on a marketing campaign dataset. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) along with Feature Engineering were conducted to prepare the dataset, understand the as well as to generate new useful features for building the model. The best model was selected by evaluating them on their accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. Once the metrics are obtained, the evaluation is repeated after tuning the hyperparameters. XGBoost was found to be the best model in building a propensity model where the hyperparameter tuning was less impactful.

articleTitle: Usability Study of Augmented Reality Training Application for Can Manufacturing Company
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This paper presents a usability study that focuses on the usability of an Augmented Reality (AR) factory manufacturing training application. This study recruited two distinct participants groups – AR developers and factory's stakeholders. This approach aimed to gather the comprehensive insights into the application's alignment with the technical and business strategies. The usability study is conducted using system usability scale (SUS) questionnaire with 12 participants. The results showed AR developers with score 50.4 and factory's stakeholders with score 57.1. The findings reveal the strengths and potential of this AR applications. From the visual aspects, AR developers complemented the 3D models that was clear and well designed and suggested improvement on the model's size in the process of viewing the machine in AR environment. The stakeholders suggested improvement on the 3D model's realism to increase the immersiveness of learning experience. In the interaction aspects, stakeholders preferred direct interaction rather than reliance of button and slider in the process AR training. Meanwhile from the business aspects, this application increases the learner's retention in the process of training. This application offers a safe and remote environment for training. In conclusion, this study evaluates the application's alignment with both technical and business strategies and the results have provided valuable insights.

articleTitle: The Development of a Web-Based Meranaw Language Lexicon Using a Rule-Based Morphological Analyzer for Meranaw Verbs: Dindiyorobasa App
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: This study introduces the “Dindiyorobasa App”, a web-based Meranaw language lexicon featuring the Rule-Based Morphological Analyzer for Meranaw Verbs (rbMAM). The app addresses critical challenges in Meranaw word analysis, minimizing over-stemming and under-stemming issues. Evaluation through the System Usability Scale (SUS) reveals an impressive score of 87.4, indicating exceptional user satisfaction and usability. The Dindiyorobasa App, with its advanced morphological analyzer, not only contributes to the preservation and revitalization of the intricate Meranaw language but also enhances the capabilities of the Meranaw-English Language Translator (MELT). The study underscores the feasibility of web-based applications in linguistics and digital preservation, providing a valuable resource for Meranaw speakers, linguists, and language enthusiasts while setting the stage for future advancements in the field.

articleTitle: UTAUT Modification Model for the Analysis of User Experience of Telemedicine Application Users in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: The emergence of Covid-19 brings opportunities to create new things post-pandemic, one of which is telemedicine. Telemedicine is a health service technology that provides long-distance health services in the form of consultations with doctors without meeting in person to provide diagnostic advice and patient care guidance. This research examines and analyzes the user experience of Halodoc and Alodokter users, two leading telemedicine applications in Indonesia. This research uses a modified UTAUT2 (Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2) model to investigate the factors that influence user acceptance and utilization of this telemedicine platform. Through a comprehensive survey and data analysis, this research aims to explain the factors that determine user satisfaction, trust and behavioral intentions towards Halodoc and Alodokter. The findings from this study contribute to a deeper understanding of user behavior and preferences in the context of telemedicine applications, providing valuable insights for improving healthcare and technology adoption in the growing field of telemedicine. We conduct questionnaire surveys using Google Forms for easy distribution among our respondents. After analyzing respondents' answers regarding related factors, it was discovered that 40.2% of respondents were used to using telemedicine, but 59.8% of respondents were still not used to using telemedicine.

articleTitle: User Interface (UI) of Singosari Temple Interactive Virtual Reality Touring System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: After the current COVID-19 pandemic, many sectors have been affected, one of which is the tourism sector. The tourism sector is at the bottom of the ranking which has experienced the most drastic decline in income. There is a positive side that can be learned from the post-pandemic conditions, several tourism sectors are starting to innovate with IT technology which has made tourism able to survive to this day. However, unfortunately, this IT technology innovation can only be implemented for tourism and medium to large scale purposes, but for tourism in local and remote areas this cannot be done due to limited human resources, facilities in the temple area and around the temple, lack of technology. support and limited marketing regarding Singosari temple. Especially for heritage tourism such as temple buildings which according to today's millennial children are less interesting to visit, because they think they are outdated and old school. This is the background for researchers to develop the application “Singosari Temple Interactive Virtual Reality Tour System for Rebranding Heritage Tourism in Malang”. This application aims to preserve Indonesian culture and help rebranding and marketing tourism, especially heritage tourism in Malang, with the help of technology, namely Virtual Reality, in accordance with suggestions from Singosari Temple experts. So it can attract the interest of not only millennial children but also all ages, from domestic to foreign visitors because bilingual languages are available. The results of this paper are that Scrum is very suitable to be implemented in this Virtual Reality research because it supports rapid change and by using the UAT testing method the average user satisfaction is 92.1% (usability aspect 91.52%, information quality aspect 90.97%, and interaction quality aspects 94.06%).

articleTitle: Behind the Scenes: An Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) on the Service Classification of the 5G/B5G Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Fifth generation and beyond (5G/B5G) is part of the next generation of mobile technology, which is expected to offer more capacity and faster speeds than the previous generation Long-Term Evolution (LTE) network. These features enable 5G/B5G to offer users a wide range of services, including smart cities, entertainment and multimedia, healthcare and mission-critical applications that benefit the entire economy and communities. However, due to growing demand, telecom service providers need to provide better Quality of service (QoS) on their networks to meet user expectations. Therefore, it is necessary to implement service classification that enables service providers to select the right network slices for each service to improve network QoS. Previous studies have predicted the classification of 5G/B5G services using traditional machine learning algorithms such as random forest and decision tree, achieving good accuracy. However, prediction based on black-box machine learning models was not transparent enough, so mobile service providers could not understand the reliability and interpretation of the results. Therefore, this article aims to model the system performance of 5G Key Performance Indicators (KPI) and extend the experiment to Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) by using the Explainable AI to look behind the scenes of the chosen black-box models for service classification of 5G/B5G networks, as this is crucial for telecom service providers to make critical investment decisions around customer and employee experience. The results from the experiments show that the random forest has the highest confidence towards class Label 3 with the probability of 35 percent.

articleTitle: Enhancing Natural Language Processing with LDA-BERT Integration: A Comprehensive Review of Methodologies, Applications, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) plays a critical role in deciphering unstructured text data. This review paper explores the integration of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) in various NLP tasks. We examine how this hybrid model enhances traditional NLP methodologies, particularly addressing the limitations of the kMeans clustering algorithm and expanding to diverse applications like sentiment analysis and topic discovery. Through an analysis of recent studies, the paper highlights the versatility and effectiveness of LDA-BERT in handling complex data structures, mitigating outlier influences, and adapting to varied data densities. The lack of standardized benchmarks for evaluating these models and their diverse application contexts are discussed as key challenges. The review emphasizes the necessity for future research to develop more uniform evaluation frameworks to better assess the effectiveness of LDA-BERT models across different NLP tasks.

articleTitle: Leveraging Mean Shift and Spectral Clustering: A Study on Crime Patterns in Los Angeles
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: In an era marked by growing complexity and interconnectivity, addressing crime is paramount for the well-being of communities worldwide. This study utilises Los Angeles Crime Data to employ clustering algorithms which are Mean Shift and Spectral Clustering, unravelling intricate crime patterns, and aiding proactive law enforcement strategies. Analysing a subset of 458,452 records from 2010 to 2019, this research identifies crime hotspots, clusters areas with similar crime trends, and extracts valuable insights into crime dynamics. Results reveal distinct patterns in crime occurrence, enabling efficient resource allocation and targeted interventions by law enforcement agencies.

articleTitle: Multi-Lingual Speaker Verification Using Malay, English, Mandarin and Tamil Languages for Door Security System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Door security system has evolved rapidly in the past twenty years, since door plays an important role on home security. Therefore, the paper proposes a door security system using multi-lingual speech recognition techniques for Malay, Chinese, Tamil and English languages. Speech is used as a tool for speech recognition since it contains features that could be trained by neural network to distinguish every voice pattern for users to perform classification. There are several factors that affects the performance of voice recognition, one of them is the background noise. This door security system that uses multi-lingual speech recognition techniques would classify the sound of the speaker by letting them voice out the name of fruits using any commonly used language in Malaysia, and the door security system will perform classification in order to identify whether the voice pattern comes from one of the users in the database. In order to implement this multi-lingual speech recognition door security system, MATLAB software is used as the development platform of this project. Besides, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) was used as the feature extraction technique and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was used as the training and matching of system while GoldWave application was used as the recording of audio signal. The experiments run on small dataset shows that the accuracy ranges from 71% to 100%.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness of Ensemble Learning for Business-to-Business (B2B) Demand Forecasting: An Empirical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is a critical component of supply chain management, particularly in Business-to-Business (B2B) settings where inventory management and production planning are essential for maintaining operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. This study explores the application of ensemble learning techniques, specifically Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Random Forest, for enhanced B2B demand forecasting. The performance of the ensemble methods is evaluated against the traditional SARIMA (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) and Holt-Winters Exponential Smoothing (HWES) model. The methodology utilizes a comprehensive dataset of transactional records and involves rigorous data preprocessing, including the creation of custom variables to augment model relevance. The ensemble learning approach demonstrates superior performance compared to the traditional methods, as evidenced by lower Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Weighted Mean Absolute Percentage Error (WMAPE) values. These findings highlight the potential of ensemble learning techniques in refining B2B demand forecasts, providing businesses with more accurate and reliable insights to optimize supply chain strategies and enhance operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Analysis of Scientific Paper Abstracts: Exploring Clustering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: The number of scientific publications published online has increased significantly in tandem with the rise of the Internet. The quantity of online articles has significantly expanded in recent years. As the quantity of scientific papers continues to grow exponentially, researchers are having challenges organising and generating relevant insights from the vast amount of information accessible. Unsupervised clustering techniques are applied in this research to categorise scientific papers based on the abstract. Centroid Based Clustering, Spectral Clustering, Distribution Based Clustering (DBSCAN), Grid Based Clustering, and hybrid LDA-BERT KMeans Clustering are the clustering algorithms explored in this study. Results showed that Centroid-Based Clustering resulted in 15 clusters with a silhouette score of 0.0038, Spectral Clustering produced 10 clusters with a silhouette score of 0.0046, DBSCAN formed a single cluster only, Grid-Based Clustering achieved 82 clusters with a silhouette score of 0.3061, and Hybrid LDA-BERT KMeans Clustering yielded 6 clusters with a silhouette score of 0.3951. Possible reasons that the algorithms are less effective compared to one another in this specific task are also investigated.

articleTitle: A Critical Review on Quality of Experience for Videos and User Engagement on Social Media Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Videos have been used to attract consumers and this has become an important marketing tool on social media platforms today. Research on users' perceptions of video Quality of Experience (QoE) has attracted increasing global attention in recent years. This paper critically reviews previous research works on factors influencing users’ perceptions of video quality on social media and the related variables. Through a systematic literature review, the paper contributes to understanding social media adoption, specifically looking into video quality and its connection to user engagement in social media advertising. The analysis of related works can highlight the gaps that have yet to be addressed.

articleTitle: Pentap: A Novel Rhythm Game with Innovative Acoustic Soundwave-based Input and Audio Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Digital Transformation and Applications (ICDXA)
abstract: Game developers constantly strive to make the player's experience more immersive by constantly innovating new ways to increase the level of interactivity of the player with the game. Different tools and methods of interaction have been innovated and developed such as motion controllers, different gamepad layouts, computer vision for body tracking and other specialized input methods. However, many of these methods come with a cost, either to the performance, accuracy or the sheer price to manufacture such a controller. Instead of developing a new hardware device, we have taken advantage of the sensors that are readily available on a mobile phone or computer device. By combining an implementation of noise cancelation and audio recognition, a possibly new revolutionary input method could be developed for rhythm games. The sounds that a player's action may make such as clapping, hitting a pen on a table or other actions are analysed through an algorithm in order to determine the input of the player. This input method that has been develop is perfectly suited for rhythm games as by nature of the rhythm game genre, sound is a crucial element for the game itself.
